subject: Interpreting the BIC for optimum k-means cluster

messages.author: a96c14dbf2761eaa
messages.subject: Interpreting the BIC for optimum k-means cluster
parts:
Hello,

I have been running DAPC analysis on a data set that includes 16 diploid and one triploid population of the genus Mimulus. The scatterplot shows a signal for 3-5 clearly defined groups (the diploid populations are clustered into three or four groups, and the triploid population is clearly separated from these diploid pops in its own group). However, the lowest BIC score suggests that I have between 17 and 20 clusters. I before running the analysis, I used the function recode.polyploids because of the two different ploidy levels.

Has anyone had a similar experience, or can suggest why the BIC score is disparate from the actual signal shown in the figure? I'd greatly listen to any advice folks can give on the matter.

-Jason Berg
U. of Maryland

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Interpreting the BIC for optimum k-means cluster
parts:
Hi Jason,

Thank you for your question. It's important to point out that DAPC is not a function from poppr. It belongs to adegenet and it's best to use that forum for your DAPC query in the future: http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/mailman/listinfo/adegenet-forum

The only function that you are using from poppr is recode_polyploids, which will remove zero-valued alleles that were used to facilitate import of polyploid samples.

Regarding your question about BIC values, perhaps this previous answer from the adegenet forum is helpful? http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/adegenet-forum/2011-June/000303.html

Best,
Zhian
